issue_paraphrase: When a Markdown setext heading (one or more text lines followed by a line of = or - characters) is written inside a blockquote, formatting collapses the heading's continuation lines onto the first line and prints the blockquote marker between the words, so `> Multi` `> Line` `> ===` becomes `> Multi > Line`. The reformatted source no longer means the same thing. Each continuation line should keep its own blockquote marker.
fix_summary: splitTextIntoSentences in src/language-markdown/print/preprocess.js now finds a 'heading' ancestor in addition to 'paragraph' when deciding how to handle an original raw line, so setext heading lines inside blockquotes are processed line by line instead of being joined with embedded blockquote markers.
notes: CLI repro is instant. The golden markdown setext suite (10 tests incl. outdent snippets) takes <1s at 1 CPU with jest-light-runner. No network needed. The fix's blockquote.md fixture only exists at the fix commit, so bring tests/format/markdown/heading/setext/ from the fix commit when running the golden test at the parent.

input file b.html: text
text
command: node bin/prettier.js b.html (parser auto-detected as html)
observed_failure_at_parent: output keeps `<span CLASS="should print as lowercase">` - the CLASS attribute on the known tag <span> is NOT lowercased, while <div> (which has per-element attribute data) is lowered to class on the same input. Fix output lowercases both to class. Golden test `snippet: #0 format 1` FAILS at parent, PASSES at fix.
verified: Both directions observed in bench-base:node-22. parent: confirmed postprocess.js contains 'ELEMENT_ATTRIBUTES.has(node.name)' (old logic) via grep before running; fix: confirmed 'HTML_TAGS.has(node.name)' present. CLI outputs differ exactly as described. Golden test run at parent with the fix's lowercase/ test dir checked in: 1 failed / 1 total; at fix: 1 passed.
install_recipe: cd <repo> && npm install ; run: node bin/prettier.js <file>. The lowercase golden test imports @prettier/html-attributes and @prettier/html-tags, which are regular dependencies installed by npm install.
issue_paraphrase: HTML attribute names are not normalized to lowercase on well-known tags that happen to lack entries in Prettier's per-element attribute table. Formatting `<span CLASS="x">` leaves the attribute name as CLASS (uppercase), while the same input on a tag like <div> is correctly rewritten to class - so the same attribute gets inconsistent casing depending on the tag. Attribute names on known HTML tags should always be lowercased.
fix_summary: normalizeName in src/language-html/parse/postprocess.js decides whether to lowercase an attribute name based on whether the element is in HTML_TAGS (known HTML tag) rather than whether it is in ELEMENT_ATTRIBUTES, and uses a null-safe per-element attribute lookup (?.) so tags without per-element attribute data still get global attributes (class, id, ...) lowercased.
notes: CLI repro instant. Golden test is a snippet-based single test that FAILS at parent (snapshot `snippet: #0 format 1`), PASSES at fix. The whole tests/format/html/attributes/lowercase/ dir is new at the fix commit - bring it over when testing at the parent. Node >= 20 needed for this test file (it uses import attributes; bench-base:node-22 is Node v22.23.2, fine).

install_recipe: cd <repo> && npm install   (at the pinned commit; this commit's package.json still declares please-upgrade-node, so a fresh install gives the CLI everything it needs). Run: node bin/prettier.js <file>
issue_paraphrase: Long SCSS @if / @else-if conditions that chain comparisons with and/or are line-broken in the wrong place: Prettier inserts a line break immediately after the == or != operator, leaving the operator alone at the end of the line and pushing its right-hand operand onto the next line. The conditions still read correctly but the break placement is inconsistent with how comparisons are normally grouped - `a == b and` should stay on one line, breaking before the next group instead.
fix_summary: printCommaSeparatedValueGroup in src/language-css/print/comma-separated-value-group.js: for SCSS control directives (@if/@else if) that also contain if/else keywords, equality/relational operators are now treated as line-break keepers, so groups like `a == b and` are printed as a unit instead of breaking after ==.
notes: CLI repro instant, one-line input. The golden atrule suite (5 files, some with snippets) takes <1s at 1 CPU. The extra failing case in if-else.scss was added by the fix commit, so bring the whole tests/format/scss/atrule/ dir from the fix commit when running the golden test at the parent. No network needed.

observed_failure_at_parent: parent output removes the quotes and prints `new(id: string): number;` (both interface and type), which turns the declared method named "new" into a TypeScript constructor/construct signature and changes the meaning of the code. Fix output keeps `"new"(id: string): number;`. Golden tests for quoteProps as-needed and consistent FAIL at parent (2 failed / 60), all pass at fix.
verified: Both directions observed in bench-base:node-22 twice: once with a HEAD-equivalent dependency set plus the please-upgrade-node shim this old commit's CLI needs, and once with a fresh `npm install` at the fix commit (which installs please-upgrade-node automatically). parent: grep confirms isKeySafeToUnquote lacks the TSMethodSignature/new guard; fix: guard present. CLI and golden tests agree in both installs.
install_recipe: cd <repo> && npm install   (at the pinned commit; pre-2026-07-24 commits declare please-upgrade-node so a fresh install provides everything). Run: node bin/prettier.js <file>
issue_paraphrase: When formatting TypeScript interfaces and object types, Prettier drops the quotes from a method literally named 'new': `"new"(id: string): number` is rewritten as `new(id: string): number`. In TypeScript an unquoted new(...) inside an interface is a construct signature (it describes how to build instances), not a method named new - so the reformatted source has a different type-level meaning than the original. The quotes on a method named new should be preserved instead of removed.
fix_summary: isKeySafeToUnquote in src/language-js/print/key.js returns false for TSMethodSignature nodes whose key value is 'new', so the quote-props machinery never unquotes that name (the same name printed via a different AST node type is still subject to the normal quote rules).
notes: CLI repro instant, 7-line input. Golden test suite quote-props has 60 tests and takes ~1s at 1 CPU; the 2 failing golden names at parent are the as-needed and consistent modes. The fixture tests/format/typescript/quote-props/issue-19618.ts and the snapshot entries were added by the fix commit - bring them from the fix commit when testing at the parent. No network needed.
